rationale: This is essentially the well-documented value×accrual-quality combination (Piotroski-style earnings-quality screening of B/M; Desai-Rajgopal-Venkatachalam), and the multiplicative rank form is a near-monotone composite rather than a true conditional screen — plus if RANK is centered rather than [0,1], the product would rank expensive high-accrual firms as high as cheap clean ones.

EBITDA/EV and cash conversion are both individually familiar, but the capital-structure-neutral multiple paired with a three-year OCF/EBITDA screen is a defensible and reasonably specific value-trap filter, though the conversion ratio is unstable for near-zero or negative EBITDA and needs a sign/denominator guard.

The MIN operator is a genuinely non-additive functional form whose conjunctive logic matches the stated hypothesis, though in practice it will correlate heavily with a simple value+quality average and compresses/ties the tails, so the incremental content over a standard double-sort is the open empirical question.

Despite being labeled cross-theme, this is a purely additive average of cash-earnings yield with two Altman-Z distress components (RE/AT, WC/AT), i.e., a rediscovery of value-screened-for-distress composites with no interaction at all, and the hypothesis's conditional language is not what the expression computes.

The ratio is non-monotone across the sign of earnings — a loss-making firm with volatile ROA scores near zero (mid-rank) while a stable loss-maker scores very negative — so the expression does not implement the stated "stable earnings make a yield more valuable" hypothesis, and winsorizing at 1% does not fix the sign discontinuity from near-zero denominators.

target_name: Industry Sales Yield With Margin Improvement
rationale: Sales-to-price (Barbee) and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) are known individually, but conditioning within-industry cheapness on a five-year gross-margin trend is a reasonable and testable directional-quality refinement; verify that IND_RANK returns non-negative values so the product does not reward the doubly-bad corner.
